title: Backwards
rule: The beats are drawn in reverse order, E5 first and E0 last, but each panel reads normally.
declares: keeps E0-E5, the four lines and the outcome
made: AGENT puppet: the 1863 telegraph operator (waistcoat, shirt sleeves) cut along drawn scissor paths into legs, torso, head and two arms, pinned with brass pins at the joints; his table and the window cut from the same plate
STRANGER puppet: the hatted woman with a hatbox from the 1867 Steinway Hall wood engraving, cut along a drawn path
engraving line printed as ink onto cream card with one threshold curve; cream scissor margin and one shadow per piece
set in the shared pen hand (HANDMADE): clock (4:10 at the answer), cupboard hinged on the left jamb with the key on its hook and SERVICE tag, SERVICE door, memo, ground lines
graphite board headers (board n, event, clock time running backwards 4:11 -> 4:08), pasted torn slips with brass pins: narration 'Before that: ...' and dialogue slips naming the speaker
storyboard sheet on the LoC 1934 sheet ground; folio '03 / Backwards' (pen99.folio)

events.board 1: E5 4:11: 4:11. He stands at the open cupboard. The key hangs there. He can't think why he came. | AGENT, to himself: ['Well, here I am...', 'and what for?']
events.board 2: E4 4:11: Before that: he opened the cupboard, and there was the key, tagged SERVICE.
events.board 3: E3 4:10: Before that: she thanked him and left the window. | STRANGER: ['Much obliged!']
events.board 4: E2 4:10: Before that: he looked up at the clock and told her. | AGENT: ['Ten past four,', 'by the clock.']
events.board 5: E1 4:10: Before that: on his way across, she stopped him at the window. | STRANGER: ['Pardon me —', 'have you the', 'right time?']
events.board 6: E0 4:09: Before that: he set off across the office for the cupboard.
events.board 7: E0 4:09: Before that: he rose from his desk.
events.board 8: E0 4:08: It began here: the memo on his desk.

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

beat: the boards pinned one by one in reading order, so the story is laid down backwards: the forgetting first, the memo last
